proposed_features.description: The primary axis of the subject's body relative to the water surface, which distinguishes horizontal swimmers from vertical divers.
The specific kinematic sequence of the arms, distinguishing the alternating over-head motion of front crawl from the simultaneous recovery of breaststroke.
The rhythmic action of the legs, distinguishing the continuous flutter kick from the whip-like kick of breaststroke or the tucked position of a dive.
The position of the head relative to the water, which is typically submerged or alternating in front crawl but frequently above water in breaststroke.
The location of the subject at the beginning of the clip, distinguishing swimmers starting in the water from divers starting on a platform or cliff.
The path of the subject through the scene, distinguishing horizontal forward motion from a vertical drop into the water.
The physical setting of the activity, which helps distinguish controlled pool environments from natural outdoor bodies of water.
The visibility of lane ropes or lines, which are characteristic of competitive or training pools but absent in natural cliff diving locations.
The temporal length of the primary action, which is typically a short, singular event for diving versus a sustained, repetitive motion for swimming.
The manner in which the subject enters the water, distinguishing a controlled dive or jump from a swimmer already in the water.
The vertical distance of the subject from the water surface at the start, which is high for cliff diving and low or zero for pool diving and swimming.
The straightness of the body, which is typically rigid and streamlined during a dive but flexed and undulating during swimming.
